description: Facing a single open from a non-blind seat: 3-bet (value+bluff) / call / fold, by hero position x opener position. Linear/value-heavy per low-stakes research.

actions.combos: TT, JJ, AQs, AJs, KQs, KJs, QJs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG raised — the strongest range at the table — and you're right behind with the whole field still to act: this is the tightest continue in the pack.
points: 3-bet (re-raise) only real value — QQ+ and AK — plus A5s as the one bluff (its ace blocks their AA/AK).
Call only a narrow, high-quality band: TT/JJ, AQs/AJs and the suited Broadways.
Everything else folds: weaker hands get dominated, and calling with 5+ players still behind invites a squeeze (a big re-raise behind you).

actions.combos: 99, TT, JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: Facing UTG's raise from UTG+2, continue tight — just a touch wider than UTG+1 would.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker bluff — UTG's raise is still the strongest range at the table.
The calls widen slightly to 99 and pick up ATs/JTs: one fewer player behind you means less risk of a squeeze (a big re-raise behind).

actions.combos: 99, TT, JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+1's raise is barely wider than UTG's and still early-position strong, so play it exactly like a UTG raise.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker; call the same 99–JJ and suited-Broadway band.
A one-notch-wider raiser doesn't justify looser calls — live players rarely open light from early seats.

actions.combos: 77-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG raised and you're in the hijack: 3-bet only real value and call a tight set of pairs and suited Broadways.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK, plus A5s as the blocker bluff.
Call 77–JJ, AQs–ATs and the suited Broadways — hands with genuine equity against a strong range.
Offsuit hands and thin suited hands fold: they're dominated too often to continue profitably here.

actions.combos: 66-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s

rationale_parts.lead: Facing a UTG raise from the cutoff, continue like the hijack does — plus a little extra width your position pays for.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK with the A5s blocker.
The calls widen down to 66 and add T9s: the players who could squeeze behind you have mostly folded, so speculative suited hands keep more of their value in position.

actions.combos: 66-TT, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, AQo

rationale_parts.lead: The hijack raises wider than UTG, so loosen your cutoff continue to match.
points: The 3-bet threshold drops to JJ+/AQs (plus AK and the A5s blocker).
AQo joins the calls — against a looser raiser, the offsuit Broadway is no longer dominated often enough to fold, especially in position.

actions.combos: TT+, AQs, AKs, AKo, A5s, A4s
22-99, AJs, ATs, A9s, KJs, KTs, QJs, QTs, JTs, T9s, 98s, AQo, AJo, KQo

rationale_parts.lead: The cutoff's raise is wide and you have the button: continue wide — position turns marginal hands into money.
points: 3-bet TT+, AQs+ and AK for value, with A5s/A4s as bluffs.
Call any pair down to 22 (set-mining pays with guaranteed position) plus the suited hands and offsuit Broadways like AJo/KQo.
From an earlier seat these calls wouldn't work — acting last every street is what makes them profitable.

actions.combos: 22-TT, AJs, ATs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s, AQo

rationale_parts.lead: The hijack raises tighter than the cutoff, so shrink your button continue accordingly.
points: The 3-bet threshold rises to JJ+ (with AQs, AK and the A5s blocker).
The weakest suited connectors drop out of the calls — a stronger raising range makes those speculative calls unprofitable even in position.

rationale_parts.lead: UTG's raise is the tightest range in the game — even on the button, this is your narrowest continue.
points: 3-bet only QQ+ and AK for value.
Call just 99–JJ, AQs, AJs and KQs.
Position helps, but it can't rescue weaker hands against a range this strong — fold them.

actions.combos: 88-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG raised and you're in the lojack: continue tight — between UTG+2's and the hijack's lines.
points: 3-bet only QQ+ and AK, plus the A5s blocker bluff.

Call 88–JJ and the AQs–ATs/suited-Broadway band: the pair floor sits one notch wider than UTG+2's (99) and one tighter than the hijack's (77) — each seat closer to the button faces one fewer possible squeezer.

actions.combos: 88-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+1's raise is barely wider than UTG's, so the lojack plays it exactly like a UTG raise.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker; call 88–JJ and the suited Broadways.
Live players rarely open light from early seats — a hair-wider raiser doesn't earn looser calls.

actions.combos: 88-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+2 opens the widest of the early seats, but it's still a strong range — keep the same disciplined continue.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker; call 88–JJ and the suited Broadways.
Their extra width is only 98s and KQo (~95% the same range) — loosening for that just adds dominated calls.

actions.combos: 77-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+1 opens essentially the same strength as UTG, so the hijack continues exactly as it would against UTG.
points: 3-bet only QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker bluff.
Call the tight 77–JJ and suited-Broadway set.

actions.combos: 77-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+2's raise is the early-to-middle transition range but still value-lean — the hijack keeps its vs-UTG shape.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker; call 77–JJ and the suited Broadways.
The raiser's small extra width (98s, KQo) doesn't make any new hand profitable with four players still behind you.

actions.combos: 77-TT, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, AQo

rationale_parts.lead: The lojack opens meaningfully wider than the early seats, so the hijack loosens to match.
points: The 3-bet threshold drops to JJ+/AQs (plus AK and the A5s blocker), and AQo enters the calls.
It stays a touch tighter than the cutoff's version of this defense (no 66, no T9s) — the hijack still has three seats plus the blinds behind it.

actions.combos: 66-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+1's raise is a near-copy of UTG's, so the cutoff continues exactly as it does against UTG.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker.
Call down to 66 and keep T9s — with only the button and blinds behind, speculative suited hands hold their value in position.

actions.combos: 66-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+2 opens the widest of the early seats but still a value-lean range — the cutoff keeps its vs-UTG continue.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK plus the A5s blocker; call 66–JJ with the suited Broadways and T9s.
The raiser's marginal extra width doesn't move any cutoff hand across the profit line.

actions.combos: 66-TT, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s, AQo

rationale_parts.lead: The lojack opens wider than the early seats, so the cutoff loosens the way it does against the hijack.
points: The 3-bet threshold drops to JJ+/AQs (plus AK and the A5s blocker), and AQo joins the calls.
T9s stays in the calls from the vs-UTG line — position keeps the speculative suited hand worth playing.

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+1's raise is essentially UTG's range one notch wider — the button treats it identically to a UTG raise.
points: 3-bet only QQ+ and AK; call the narrow 99–JJ, AQs, AJs, KQs band.
Even the button's positional edge doesn't rescue weaker hands against an early-position range this strong.

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+2's raise is still a strong early-position range, so the button keeps the same narrow continue as against UTG.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK; call 99–JJ, AQs, AJs and KQs.
Their small extra width (98s, KQo) doesn't make your next-best hands (88, ATs, KJs) profitable against a range that's still tight and value-heavy.

actions.combos: 22-TT, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s, AQo

rationale_parts.lead: The lojack's raise is wide enough that the button plays it like a slightly tighter hijack raise: continue wide.
points: 3-bet JJ+/AQs and AK with the A5s blocker.
Call any pair 22–TT — set-mining pays in position with only the blinds behind — plus the suited Broadways, T9s and AQo.
